en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. (Note: As spotted by AppleVis Community Member TJT 2001 , Apple has also released iOS/iPadOS 26.7 for those not wishing to upgrade to iOS 27.) This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. iOS 27 Release Notes iOS 27 introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as well as new features to help parents create safe digital experiences for kids, and improvements that make iOS more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. The next generation of Apple Intelligence also powers new features across apps that simplify the things you do every day, like editing images in Photos, communicating in Messages and Mail, and browsing in Safari. New parental controls and significant updates to Screen Time make it more intuitive and easy to use, so parents can feel confident that they're building the right digital experience for their child. And with improvements that span design, performance, connectivity, search, and more, the experience on iOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what's in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food. Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you've written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you've previously used in your conversations with those people. Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Photos. Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position. Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject. Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits. Safari. Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together. Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability. Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website's content or formatting. All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions. Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one. Home. Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification. Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what's happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers. Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan. Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence. Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Accessibility. VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration. An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions. A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation. Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like "tap the gear" or "tap the button in the top right". And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Child Safety Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child. Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it. Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child's age. Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends. Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps. System Improvements Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted . Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers. Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks. And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/ Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 AppleVis iOS 27 Content AppleVis has the following content available for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Blog Post: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements Blog Post: What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users , by Scott Davert Podcast: An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 , by Michael Hansen Podcast: A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 , by David Nason Podcast: A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 , by Levi Gobin How to Update iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users
en.summary: Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories . Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with. A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community. Changes for VoiceOver and Braille Users Improved Image and Screen Descriptions As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can. New Verbosity Options for Coding With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings. New "Actions" rotor for trackpad users With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it. "Ducking Amount" setting The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound. Braille Improvements While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, text field labels can now be shown in braille. You can change the format these labels are presented in, or hide them entirely, by going to VoiceOver Utility > Braille > Layout, and clicking Text Field Labels. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Braille Access in macOS Golden Gate supports plain text (txt) and portable document format (PDF) files. Improvements for Low Vision Users While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, content in Accessibility Reader can now be summarized and translated while retaining its original formatting on macOS Golden Gate. If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate. Other Changes As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the Aaron (English US), Arthur (English UK), Catherine (English Australia), Gordon (English Australia), and Martha (English UK) voices have been reintroduced with macOS Golden Gate. Like other voices, they can be used with Siri, as well as for accessibility functions like VoiceOver and Read & Speak. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, subtitles for spoken dialog in videos where captioning is not already provided can be generated automatically in macOS Golden Gate. These can be turned on and adjusted when playing a video by clicking the "show legible media selection menu" button in the playback controls group. Writing Tools, previously accessed from many apps' Edit menus, as well as many text fields' context menus, is now accessed with VoiceOver by focusing on a text field and choosing "Show Writing Tools" from the Actions Menu. When toggling Cursor Tracking with VO-F3, its state is reflected in the "Mouse pointer:" popup menu in VoiceOver Utility. In prior versions of macOS, the state of Cursor Tracking was not reflected in this popup menu, which had the potential to confuse users. Change List In its support documentation, Apple lists the following changes for VoiceOver users in macOS Golden Gate: You can now turn off announcements that webpages send automatically, such as live scores, new messages, or status updates. Turn off Enable Web Announcements to silence announcements from a single area of a webpage or from the entire page. VoiceOver remembers your choice for that website, so the area stays silent the next time you visit. With the new Coding tab in the Verbosity category of VoiceOver Utility, you can choose whether VoiceOver announces line numbers, and whether it plays a tone or speaks a description when it encounters an error, a breakpoint, or the program counter. Bug Fixes and New Bugs for VoiceOver Users Below are lists of the bugs we believe to have been resolved in macOS Golden Gate, as well as new bugs introduced in this release. We strongly recommend that you read through the list of new bugs and any replies before updating, as this will allow you to make an informed decision on whether to install macOS Golden Gate or wait for a future release. While we are confident in the status of issues contained in this post, we do not claim that our bug list is definitive or that our assessments are infallible. Some issues may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features, and the number of available configurations and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and it is also likely that you will encounter issues that we did not experience during our own testing and daily use of macOS Golden Gate. To ensure the information here is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed macOS Golden Gate. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it's even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they're already aware of the ones listed here. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. Accessibility Bugs Resolved in macOS Golden Gate To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or Braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to macOS Golden Gate. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in macOS Tahoe have been resolved or meaningfully improved in macOS Golden Gate: VoiceOver no longer speaks list items on webpages unreliably. Pauses between sentences are no longer extended when using VoiceOver's "Say All" command. It is once again possible to reply to a message in the Message app by selecting the "Reply" action in the Actions menu. The Actions menu for Messages in the Messages app no longer contains redundant tapback actions. New Bugs for VoiceOver Users in macOS Golden Gate Our testing suggests that the following bugs have been introduced in macOS Golden Gate: After clicking the “Proofread” button in the Writing Tools popover using VoiceOver, only the Next, Previous, and Close buttons are visible, with no way to view the specific changes made to the text. There is no way to open or redownload apps from the “Apps & Purchases” page in the App Store using VoiceOver, with each app conveyed only as a button with no actions available and nothing to interact with besides the app’s name. To redownload a previously purchased app, you must click the [app name] button to open the product page, and then click the "Redownload" button in the toolbar. The sections and buttons in Safari’s Page Menu lack accessibility labels. Interacting with a section and pressing VO-Space on an item (all of which are clearly labeled) works to activate the item; however, interacting with each item in a section reveals an unlabeled button. When playing audio or video, VoiceOver announces “system has new window” once the media has started playing. The identity and purpose of this window is not clear from this announcement, and no new items appear in the application or window chooser menus. Other Possible Bugs In addition to the bugs listed here, we strongly recommend you read this Megathread about the macOS Golden Gate RC , , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software that may differ from our own. macOS Golden Gate release notes macOS 27 introduces Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence, new parental controls, and an expansive set of improvements that make your Mac even more responsive, reliable, and delightful. Experience the new Siri AI Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings. Take action on what’s onscreen With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space. Powerful new ways to edit photos Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex. New tools to browse in Safari Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes. Easily create Shortcuts using natural language With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic. Even more refined design Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design. New child safety features Powerful new parental controls help parents manage what content their children see, who they can communicate with, and when they can access apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage kids’ time in apps across categories. Schedules manage which apps kids can access at different times of day and throughout the week. A more responsive and delightful experience An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable. Learn more Discover even more powerful capabilities in the next release by visiting apple.com/os/macos . For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100 . Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability . Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence . Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039 . In Conclusion We would like to thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. We'd love to hear your thoughts after you've had a chance to install the upgrade. What new features do you find most useful? Are there any changes you don't like? Please share your feedback in the comments below. When doing so, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in macOS Golden Gate. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we thank Apple's Accessibility team for their prompt response in fixing many of the bugs reported during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle. However, many longstanding issues remain unresolved, and we find the inability to fully use the Proofread function, a key feature of Apple Intelligence, during a cycle where enhancements to Apple Intelligence were heavily emphasized, incredibly disappointing. We encourage Apple to promptly address this and other outstanding accessibility issues discussed in this post and the comments below so that macOS can be as accessible, usable, and enjoyable as possible for all users. To install macOS Golden Gate, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Upgrade Now button to begin the upgrade process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. More information on how to update the software on your Mac is available on this Apple Support page.

en.title: watchOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver Features, Issues, and Improvements
en.summary: Apple has today released watchOS 27 to the public. watchOS 27 is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later and the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later. Due to the inherent challenges of beta software testing on watchOS, our testing of watchOS 27 has been quite limited. That said, for VoiceOver users, there is at least one new bug that we are aware of and a handful of new features and improvements. New VoiceOver Bugs in watchOS 27 There is rather significant latency with VoiceOver speech when swiping through the user interface. Specifically, there is a delay between when the VoiceOver sound effects/haptics play, and when VoiceOver speaks. Our testing suggests that this issue is not synthesizer-specific. It is unclear to us whether this behavior is simply a function of the newer operating system encountering the limits of hardware (something that has historically been a challenge on Apple Watch devices), or whether this is something that can be resolved by Apple in a future software update. A Feedback report has been filed, and we will keep the community advised as additional information becomes available. If you identify any additional vision accessibility bugs in watchOS 27, please let us know by posting a comment. New VoiceOver Features and Improvements in watchOS 27 There is a new "Tap to Wake" toggle in VoiceOver settings. By default, the setting is enabled, and the Watch will be woken when you tap on the screen. Our best understanding is that disabling this feature should prevent the device from waking when the screen is tapped. It is now possible to customize the speaking of VoiceOver hints in watchOS. Available options are 'Always', 'Never', and 'App-Specific Hints'. On the Clock Face, VoiceOver now speaks the names of Complications before speaking their content. For example, VoiceOver might say, "Weather, Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees," instead of just saying "Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees." For braille display users, there is a new setting, "Translate After a Delay." There are other braille settings that we also believe may be new in this release, but our braille-related testing in watchOS is very limited and so this is not something we are able to comment on with any level of certainty. If you spot any other new features/changes in watchOS 27 or have any corrections to the above, please do let us know by posting a comment. watchOS 27 Release Notes watchOS 27 features the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, updates to Workout Buddy, a new tap gesture, a dynamic app grid to make it easier to access your most used apps, and improvements that make watchOS 27 more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. With improvements that span areas like fitness, design, performance, and more, the experience on watchOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on paired iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Apple Intelligence across apps Workout Buddy delivers motivation with new insights and is now available without your iPhone nearby when you have a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you’re speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Cycle Tracking Cycle deviation notifications that are suggestive of perimenopause can be received by those age 40 and over. Watch Faces Siri Modular face features a rectangular complication that mirrors the top widget of the Smart Stack, which dynamically updates to show the most relevant widget, as well as a Siri complication to quickly invoke Siri. Smart Stack Single-handed tap gesture enables you to tap your index finger and thumb together once to select a widget in the Smart Stack, even if your other hand is occupied. New suggestion widgets will be surfaced when most relevant to you, including a Parked Car location, birthday reminders for a close contact, balance changes on a transit card, Noise app after a loud noise notification, and more. System Improvements Dynamic app grid highlights your most popular and recently used apps. Find My app is now consolidated into one app to show People, Devices, and Items with a map-centric interface. Media playback now starts faster. Workout app makes distance calculations during treadmill workouts even more accurate from the first step of every walk or run. Fitness app features more accurate route maps after workouts. Battery extension notifications may be proactively offered to disable certain features to increase battery life, including gestures, Start Workout reminders, and Raise to Speak method of invoking Siri. Shazam in the Smart Stack and Music Recognition app identifies songs offline without an internet connection and delivers results automatically when you’re back online. Liquid Glass refinements improve readability with more uniform refraction and improved contrast. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 How to Update watchOS 27 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.

en.title: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 were released to the public on Monday, September 14, 2026. This post contains a summary of new bugs and fixes impacting VoiceOver and Braille support that the AppleVis Editorial Team has independently validated during our use and testing of these releases. The information contained in this post is compiled from our own use and testing of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 during the beta period from June to September 2026; as well as from validated reports submitted by others through our Community Bug Program and shared on the AppleVis Forum. Our sincere appreciation goes to everyone who so generously took the time to share their findings with us. At the outset, we need to state explicitly that the bug list contained in this post is not definitive and that our assessments are not infallible. While we are confident in the presence of the issues discussed in this post, there are many other reports shared on the AppleVis Forum by members of our community that we have not been able to independently replicate with the available information. Many of these reports represented use cases that are different from those of our team; and a small number were issues that, despite understanding how to reproduce them, we did not get the same results. We say all of this so that readers understand the limits of our own testing, and that others' experiences may be different from ours. An issue not being present in our bug list does not mean the issue does not exist; it simply means that we are either unaware of or unable to reproduce it. As is our routine practice, each bug in this post has been given a severity rating. These ratings are based upon what we believe to be the implications for accessing and using features and functionality for the average user; the level of impact on the overall user experience; and whether or not there is an effective workaround for the issue. However, as these ratings are subjective to an extent, it is very possible that they may not reflect your own opinion or use case. With this in mind, we strongly recommend reading this full post and any replies before updating to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27; as we believe this will help you make an informed decision on whether to install the software at the current time or to wait for a future release. We also strongly recommend that you read this Megathread about the iOS 27 RC , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software. Some issues listed in this post and on the Forum may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features and the number of devices, available configurations, and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and you likely will not agree with every severity rating for the bugs that you do experience. While we wish it were otherwise, this is to be expected. And as is the nature with all software, it is also likely that you will encounter issues that are not reported in this post. To ensure the information in this post is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it is even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they are already aware of the ones listed in this post. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. With all of the preamble out of the way, below are the new bugs for VoiceOver and Braille users which members of the AppleVis Editorial Team have personally experienced and believe to be present in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Major Change to VoiceOver's Audio Profile In iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, there is a significant change in the sound profile of VoiceOver when the device's internal speaker is used. When compared to iOS 26, VoiceOver audio in iOS 27 has significantly less bass, particularly at lower volume levels. The resulting sound might best be described as 'neutral' or 'flat', with significantly less of the low-end emphasis and other processing that has characterized VoiceOver audio in recent versions of iOS/iPadOS. If you have not yet upgraded to iOS 27, we believe that you can get a reasonable approximation of how VoiceOver will sound on your device by making a phone call, putting the call on speaker, and then using VoiceOver to navigate around the screen; as the flatter, more neutral sound profile that VoiceOver uses during a phone call sounds very similar to what we are hearing in iOS 27. At the time of publication, we do not know whether the change to VoiceOver's sound profile is expected behavior; thus, we are not including it in our bug list. Nevertheless, we feel that users should be aware of this change before upgrading. If we receive additional information, we will update this post accordingly. Serious Bugs When the state of an item changes or the screen updates, VoiceOver does not always recognize/speak the information. This issue has many manifestations, including (but not limited to): When waking the device, VoiceOver may speak the time the device was last woken rather than the current time; When information updates onscreen (such as the status of an operation in an app), VoiceOver may not speak it right away and instead speak the previously displayed text. There is no known workaround, though VoiceOver will eventually speak the updated information if focus is moved off of and back onto the impacted element enough times. The VoiceOver Per-Voice Equalizer (a feature that allows one to customize certain frequency/tonal characteristics of a voice) does not work. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the per-voice Equalizer, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. The VoiceOver Pronunciation Dictionary does not work reliably, with custom pronunciations often not being obeyed by VoiceOver. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the Pronunciation Dictionary, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. On some devices, Sound Curtain and Touch Curtain do not work. For affected users, it is possible to partially work around the issue with Sound Curtain by setting the device volume to 0%. There is no known workaround for Touch Curtain. If you rely on Sound Curtain or Touch Curtain, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. If an external audio device is connected, VoiceOver speech does not work when playing audio in Safari. Pausing the audio causes it to start working again. Sometimes, when reading text, VoiceOver stops speaking and does not resume on its own. This issue does not occur all of the time. When it does occur, speech will stop mid-sentence (and sometimes even mid-word). Touching the screen or performing a touch gesture (like a one-finger swipe left or right) restores speech, and the user can then refocus VoiceOver on the impacted element. In iOS 27's new Recovery Menu, there is no spoken feedback in Diagnostics Mode, rendering this option completely inaccessible. There is no known workaround to make Diagnostics Mode itself usable. If you do manage to accidentally get your device into Diagnostics Mode, our experience is that the device will restart into normal operation after approximately five to ten minutes of inactivity. Moderate Bugs In Safari, the buttons to switch between the Start Page, Reading List, History, and Bookmarks do not work. It is possible to select these buttons, and VoiceOver indicates they have been selected, but the content itself does not update, meaning content cannot be reached. As a workaround, perform a one-finger triple-tap (what is known as a "long press") on the desired button to activate it. Our thanks to AppleVis user Brian Giles for this workaround. When VoiceOver focus is placed inside a text field, and then subsequently moved onto a combo box, the menu automatically opens. On occasions, when swiping through the Lock Screen using one-finger swipe right or left, VoiceOver focus may be inconsistent. When navigating through the Lock Screen using a one-finger swipe right, after the "Swipe up to Unlock" element, the expected behavior is that VoiceOver will focus on the first notification (if present); Focus status (if present); or the first item on the screen, like Flashlight or Camera. However, sometimes, VoiceOver users may find that focus is instead placed on items from the Status Bar, such as Cellular Carrier, Battery Percentage, or the Clock. If VoiceOver focus does land on items from the Status Bar when swiping, it is sometimes possible to continue swiping to the right and get to the first Lock Screen item; however, other times, VoiceOver focus can become stuck in a loop between the time, the "Swipe Up to Unlock" element, Cellular Carrier, an element with no spoken or audible feedback, or any combination of the above. Sometimes, VoiceOver does not speak the time when the device is woken with the Side Button. If this issue occurs, single-tap the screen with one finger to wake the device. After prompting Siri with the Side button, revealing the interface at the top of the screen, nothing happens when double-tapping the "Open in App" button. Double-tapping this button should work to activate it, opening the conversation in the Siri app. In the Phone App, the buttons to switch between 'All' and 'Missed' do not work. This issue can be worked around by either switching to Unified View or swiping through all calls in Classic View. Sometimes, it is not possible to access notifications with VoiceOver that are visually displayed onscreen. Typically, the 'Show notifications' button is present, but on these intermittent occasions, selecting it fails to reveal the notifications, and does nothing. If this issue occurs, double-tap and hold on the "Show Notifications" button, and swipe up. This will reveal the notifications. VoiceOver's 'Copy Speech' function copies the full semantic markup and hints, instead of just the spoken text. For example, in iOS 27, Copy Speech might paste "Latest news, heading Level 2". In previous versions of iOS, Copy Speech would only paste "Latest news," which is the desired behavior. Screen Recognition does not appear in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel, even if selected for inclusion. The Camera App contains extraneous elements for editing Camera Controls when Edit Mode is not active. This includes "Remove" elements next to each camera control and a "Done" button that does nothing when tapped. When an app is open and VoiceOver focus is placed on the battery indicator, it is not possible to swipe to other items on the status bar. The Direct Touch option in the VoiceOver Quick Settings panel does not work. Minor Bugs In Notification Center, the Rotor Action for clearing all notifications does not work. As a workaround, Locate and double-tap on the "Clear, Notification Center" button, then double-tap on the "Confirm Clear, Notification Center" button that appears. Our thanks to AppleVis Community member Sieghard Weitzel for this workaround. On the Keypad in the Phone app, the button to place the call is labeled as "Call Answer." When focusing on a conversation in the Siri app, the Actions rotor for the conversation contains two identical "Delete" actions. When the device is set to 24-Hour Time, VoiceOver does not correctly speak the time on the top of the hour. When customising VoiceOver touch gestures and you select to replace the current command with a new one, the old command is sometimes not overwritten, necessitating manual removal and replacement. When the Safari toolbar is set to 'Bottom', the "Show Bookmarks" button is incorrectly labelled as "Bookmark." When the VoiceOver cursor reaches the first or last element onscreen in the Camera app, focus loops instead of stopping at the boundary. Improvements for VoiceOver and Braille in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in iOS/iPadOS 26 have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Stability of VoiceOver focus has been significantly improved across the operating system. The screen no longer locks while VoiceOver is reading a notification on the Lock Screen. Keyboard sounds once again play when VoiceOver is on, regardless of the audio ducking setting. VoiceOver focus is no longer erratic in the App Switcher when it is opened from the Home Screen. The default volume of the Eloquence speech synthesizer more closely matches that of other voices. In Conclusion Our team has compiled lists of new vision accessibility bugs for every major iOS and iPadOS release since iOS 7 in 2013. No software from any manufacturer is completely free of bugs. That said, the number of bugs - particularly those classified as "serious" and involving core VoiceOver and braille functionality - in iOS/iPadOS 27 is deeply concerning. We call on Apple to urgently prioritize fixing the bugs listed in this post, as well as those on The AppleVis Bug Tracker . If you have not already upgraded to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27, we would strongly recommend that you take a few moments to read through any replies to this post before doing so; in case other users' experiences differ from our own. Also, consider that historically, Apple has delivered fixes for many accessibility bugs within the first few x.x.1 updates following major releases, and waiting briefly may allow Apple to resolve any initial problems reported after the public release. In the event that you do encounter an issue that is particularly bothersome, there are some troubleshooting steps you can take. Sometimes, simply toggling VoiceOver off and on again or restarting your device can resolve some issues that may arise following an OS update. Therefore, we highly recommend including these steps as part of your standard troubleshooting process. If restarting VoiceOver and/or your device does not resolve the issue, it might be worth considering a reset of your VoiceOver Settings; to do this, navigate to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Reset VoiceOver Settings. While this approach requires manually reconfiguring your customized VoiceOver settings, we have heard of multiple instances where a VoiceOver settings reset resolved issues since this feature became available in last year's iOS 26. This suggests that occasionally, problems can be attributed to local factors rather than being OS bugs. Finally, when commenting below, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we would like to again thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the iOS/iPadOS 27 beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute.

en.summary: New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you. Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime. Questions span a wide range of categories — General Knowledge, Science & Nature, History, Geography, Sports, and Arts & Entertainment — so you'll always find something that suits your interests and adds to what you know. And when a hard question comes your way, you have tools to help: remove half the options with 50:50, swap a question that doesn't suit you, or grant yourself a few extra seconds. The more you win, the higher you climb through the levels and the more coins you collect — and each day you can spin the daily wheel for a free reward. The game is made for everyone to enjoy: it works smoothly with TalkBack and VoiceOver, so screen reader users get a complete experience, crafted to be heard and not only seen. Add your friends, exchange messages between matches, and discover together who deserves the title of the smartest. Play in Arabic or English, and switch languages whenever you wish. So, are you ready to compete? Your next opponent is waiting on your move. Heading

en.title: What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users
en.summary: Introduction 15 years ago, I produced my first "What's New in iOS Accessibility" article. Every September since, I've been documenting what my testing of the betas has yielded. There are many welcome mainstream changes in this year's iOS 27, such as the upgraded Siri app, new parental controls, a slider to adjust Liquid Glass, further enhanced Apple Intelligence features, and much more. The new Siri has its own app, and coverage of it is beyond the scope of this article other than to mention it's much more versatile and can assist with all kinds of tasks from asking about your personal data to recipes and so on. Lots of individuals will be reviewing these new features. As I've done for many years now, I'm documenting my findings after testing the new version of iOS throughout the summer to discuss accessibility-specific features which impact blind and DeafBlind users. Following what has become a tradition, Apple began discussing enhancements coming to accessibility with its announcement ahead of Global Accessibility Awareness Day. More info about forthcoming features was detailed during the Worldwide Developers Conference Keynote. Devices that will work with iOS 27, according to Apple, are the iPhone SE 2 and later, as well as the iPhone 11 and later. The page linked to above is also a good resource for mainstream changes coming in iOS 27. VoiceOver Though there are fewer changes in iOS 27 than what were found in iOS 26, VoiceOver has gained quite a bit of new functionality. Whether you are a speech user or a braille one, there are a lot of new offerings in this year's release. Pronounce It Together There is now a setting which allows a VoiceOver user to import or share their pronunciation dictionary. This feature could be helpful when, for example, text-to-speech engines do not pronounce things correctly in local dialects. Instead of everyone having to make the changes, one person could compile it and share it with other users in a similar situation. It could also be used as a form of prank. Imagine changing the pronunciation of a friend's name to a friendly insult along with other changes and they later encounter it. These settings can be found under Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Speech> Pronunciations. Selecting 'Import' will bring up the Files function and allow the user to browse to the file they wish to import. Sharing one's own pronunciations brings up the standard Share Sheet, where the file can be sent to any number of places or contacts. Hide Your Cursor For those who may not be aware, the VoiceOver cursor appears as a black rectangular outline surrounding the item that currently has VoiceOver focus. While handy in some situations such as showing a sighted user where VoiceOver focus is set, helping a low vision user who tracks VoiceOver focus, or when demonstrating VoiceOver support to a developer, there are certainly reasons individuals may wish to disable it. This is because it can also serve as a distraction when the VoiceOver cursor itself isn't an important part of the iPhone's purpose. For example, when using the iPhone for face-to-face communication as a DeafBlind user, it can distract the person you are attempting to communicate with from the text you are typing. Some may wish to hide the visual VoiceOver cursor during screen sharing. To adjust this setting, head to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Cursor Visibility, and choose from showing the cursor, hiding it always, or hiding it during screen sharing. Navigating in New Ways with Explore By Touch iOS 27 brings new options to precisely control VoiceOver's reading of text when using Explore by Touch, or, as it's more commonly referred to, 'dragging your finger around the screen'. Options for Text Exploration are now Paragraph, Line, or Sentence. For example, when set to 'Sentence', VoiceOver will only speak the sentence under your finger instead of the entire element as it previously did. Users can adjust this by going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Text Exploration. Note that changes made in Text Exploration only apply to Explore by Touch, and will not impact swiping through content. At least, not this particular setting. It's for Swipers Too A separate setting, called Text Navigation, offers the ability to modify how VoiceOver moves when swiping left and right through the screen with one finger. The available options are Line, Sentence, Paragraph, and Element. In addition to allowing one to more easily read blocks of text that VoiceOver sees as one large element, having these two new sets of options can give VoiceOver users other choices than the rotor for text navigation. To check out the new settings for swiping, head to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Text Navigation. Remember that you will need to adjust settings for Text Exploration and Text Navigation separately. Hints Become Customizable For a lot of the clients I work with who use speech, the hints offered by VoiceOver can be helpful, but there comes a point where they cause interference with touchscreen navigation once a user advances in their journey of learning VoiceOver. For example, "Double Tap to Open" can grind on one's nerves after a while. When I first started learning to use an iPhone with iOS 4, this was also something I became frustrated with. If the system hints become a nuisance, the user now has more control over them. iOS 27 brings the ability to adjust the amount of delay between when VoiceOver provides active information about what is in focus and when the hint will be conveyed. To configure this, head to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Verbosity> Hints, and then either type the duration in seconds ranging from 0.05 to 2.0, or use the 'Decrement' and 'Increment' buttons. The default is 0.8 seconds. It's also now possible to specify if users want all hints, app-specific hints, or no hints at all. You can find these options on the same screen. No Modifier Required for These Functions For VoiceOver commands to be assigned to keyboard shortcuts, Bluetooth keyboard users have always had to include their chosen VoiceOver modifier along with the command. This is no longer necessary with the function keys located in the top row of many Bluetooth keyboards. The setting must be enabled, which one can do by going to Settings>Accessibility>VoiceOver>Commands and setting the Switch Button for "No Modifier Keys" to on. Instead of having to press, for example, VoiceOver Modifier f8 to launch the VoiceOver Settings menu, users can now simply press F8. Live and Open for Questions Live Recognition was first integrated into VoiceOver with iOS 18. iOS 27, coupled with Apple Intelligence, gives Live Recognition even more power. Activating the 'Ask' button will allow the user to ask about what is currently in the camera's view. It's also possible to tell Live Recognition to focus on a specific thing in your environment. As long as that item is able to be tracked, its actions and movements will often be reported by VoiceOver. Ask is a feature that is highly customizable. Going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Live Recognition allows the user to set up some other options. One can change the default question asked when the button is activated, make the default input either dictation or typing, and have the Volume buttons take a still photo for a follow-up or more detailed description. Ask can be set up with a gesture, Bluetooth keyboard command, the Accessibility Shortcut, or a Perkins-style keyboard command. If none of those are what the user wants, there is also the ability to launch the Ask feature using the Action Button. It can be enabled by going to Settings> Action Button, selecting the Accessibility category, and then choosing 'Ask a Question'. The View From iOS In my view, pardon the pun, the largest upgrade for VoiceOver and braille users in iOS 27 is the massive overhaul of the Image Recognition feature. This is thanks to Apple Intelligence, but I'm sure those using iPhone 15 and earlier devices aren't feeling very thankful, since they do not have access to these features. Unlike the multi-step processes involved with using third-party services for detailed descriptions, Image Recognition descriptions typically take less than three seconds. They can be generated on virtually all images the iPhone encounters, and the user does not need to download or upload each image they wish to have described. It is also possible to describe the screen of the device itself, to ask questions about the image in focus, and to generate a description with the ability to ask a follow-up question immediately. These features can be activated through the VoiceOver rotor or by adding specific functions to gestures. The two devices I have upgraded at this point had the Image Recognition options in the Rotor. If, by chance, your Rotor does not have the Image Recognition option after upgrading, it can be added by going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Rotor> Rotor Items and selecting Image Recognition. Since there are up to seven different options for Image Recognition, Apple has also given users the ability to add and remove what they wish to this rotor item. It can be configured by going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Rotor> Image Recognition Rotor. Each of the available options will be discussed below. Image/Item Description will allow the user to get a description of the image or item that VoiceOver focus is set to. Based on my testing, it is generated in less than three seconds. It will be delivered in the form of a VoiceOver announcement. For those using braille, one can read the description at their own pace by pressing Space with N. When done, pressing space with n will return the user to where they were before. I find this particular function to be wonderful for generating descriptions of things in my Facebook feed, my growing photo library, album art in the Music app, and when reading photo-heavy articles on various news sources. Interestingly, this function is the only one that can be mapped to a Perkins-style keyboard. The other options discussed below are not available for users of Perkins-style keyboards. Using the Copied Speech Rotor option launched with iOS 26, users can copy the description to wherever they want on their iOS device. A simpler solution in some situations is available as discussed below. Ask About Image/Item is another option, which does exactly what the choice says. After selecting this, users are presented with a text field which allows them to type a question. Pressing return or enter will generate a response. The nice thing is that you do not need to generate a general description before asking a question. Placing VoiceOver focus on the image is all that is required. With many third-party applications, one must first wait through getting the general description before they can ask a question. I have solved simple CAPTCHAs by asking my iPhone to provide me with only the text in the image. I can then copy it and solve CAPTCHAs. I have not tried more complex puzzles. Explore Image/Item allows you to get the same description as you get when generating an Intelligent Description, but it is static text instead of a VoiceOver announcement. After the text description, there is an option to ask a question either by typing or voice. Also, when focus is on the description, one can flick up with one finger, or use whatever alternative method, to copy the description. Ask About Screen allows the user to get a description of the screen on their iOS device. It functions the same as the Ask About Image/Item choice, but covers the entire screen. I've found this feature handy for understanding what buttons without labels in applications do. This is far more preferable to activating the button to see what happens. The other two options are Describe Screen and Explore Screen. These work the same as the others documented above, only this applies to your entire screen instead of one item. I mentioned browsing photos above, and when in the Photos app, there is yet another rotor option available called Save Intelligent Image Description. When selected, this will add the description generated to the photo itself which will then be available later. A final setting is the ability to show a list of the recognition options discussed above. It does not have a touch screen gesture assigned to it, but the user can create one. On a Bluetooth keyboard, pressing VoiceOver Modifier, Shift, and R will bring up this menu. Sorry, braille display users, there appears to be no Perkins-style keyboard option. Automatic Image Descriptions Users can head to Settings>Accessibility>VoiceOver>VoiceOver Recognition>Image Descriptions to configure whether image descriptions are provided automatically. One can configure whether they want automatic image descriptions or whether they are conveyed as a fallback when images have alt text. Note that this setting applies to the classic image descriptions, but one will not receive a detailed description such as the ones provided by Apple Intelligence. Braille There are some changes to braille outlined below. As a general usage note, writing longer passages of text seems to be a bit more reliable than it was in all of the iOS 26 releases. Further, there were some issues in iOS 26 with cursor routing buttons not routing correctly and focus jumping back to the top in longer blocks of text while the user was reading. Based on my use, all of these issues have been improved significantly. Predict More Predictably with Braille Screen Input Braille Screen Input now uses the same Predictive Text gestures as the default onscreen keyboard. When typing on the standard touchscreen keyboard, iOS uses Autocorrect and Predictive Text to identify the word you probably intended based on the letters entered, nearby keys, sentence context, and commonly-used language. Braille Screen Input now uses this same prediction system: after entering a word, users can swipe up or down with one finger to move through suggested words or corrections, then continue typing once the desired suggestion is selected. Further, it is now possible to type part of an emoji name and swipe up or down with one finger to find it. Functionality of the BSI Autocorrect requires the primary software keyboard Autocorrect setting to be enabled in Settings> General> Keyboards. Finally, iOS 27 adds the ability to more easily insert alternative characters. To activate alternative character selection, hold the dots of the character you wish to insert until you hear a sound, then release and swipe up or down with one finger to select the desired symbol. A More Flexible Cursor Shifting to braille display users, there is a new setting called 'Snap To Print Text Cursor', which can be found by going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Braille> Cursor Routing. The options are the new Snap To Text Cursor or Any Braille Cell. By default, Snap To Print Text Cursor was selected when I upgraded. The 'Snap to Print Text' setting places the cursor on the closest print text equivalent even when contracted braille is enabled. This setting is particularly helpful for those braille display users using QWERTY keyboards to type while also using contracted braille for reading, as it removes some ambiguity from where the cursor is located. Text Field Labels That Stick Prior to iOS 27, when activating a text field, the text label would disappear entirely. In iOS 27, the label persists even when the text field is active. The label itself appears between two indicator symbols which clearly distinguish the label from the text entered. It can be configured by going to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Braille> Text Field Labels. The options are to show an abbreviated version of the label or the full thing. Selecting 'Collapse' will provide two indicators without the text label. Selecting 'Full' will display the entire text field label. You can collapse the label by pressing a cursor routing button. If you disable everything in this menu, the behavior will be as it always was in past versions of iOS. Braille Access Expands File Support Braille Access now supports plain text and PDF files. As such, the formerly named 'BRF Files' is now simply called 'Files'. To import these file types, users can follow the same procedures they already use to get BRF content imported. Files are still stored in the 'BRF files' folder on iCloud, so any method a user would utilize to copy text and PDF content is the same. I found that opening plain text files worked quickly, and it was nice to have them imported. Unlike many applications for braille readers, Braille Access tends to remember the place I was in a file when I open it again. PDF content will display, but seems to depend on how well the creator of the file treated accessibility. Formatting such as headings is not preserved. There also appears to be a file size limit, as I was not able to load a PDF file that was 15 MB due to the images it contained. New Features Bring New Keyboard Shortcuts Apple has added a few new options for Perkins-style keyboard shortcuts that people may take advantage of. Under the VoiceOver category, one has been added for launching the Ask function found in VoiceOver Recognition, while another was added for generating an Intelligent Description with Image Recognition. There are no new commands for the other Image Recognition options discussed above. Another mapping option was made available for ignoring trackpads. Hearing On-demand Sign Language Interpreters on FaceTime As part of Apple's Global Accessibility Awareness Day announcement in May, the company shared preliminary details of an API that providers of sign language interpretation apps could use to allow callers to add an interpreter to their FaceTime call. As of the time of writing, there do not appear to be any announcements concerning providers utilizing this API, but hopefully that will come soon. Auto-Caption This Video Captioning automatically produces synchronized subtitles from spoken audio when a video has no existing captions. Apple says it works with videos recorded on the iPhone, videos sent to the user, streamed videos, and other uncaptioned videos played through supported system playback interfaces. When I enabled captioning in the Photos app while playing a video, there were several visual options available for adjusting the output. However, I was not able to find the generated captions with braille. Thankfully, Live Captions under Braille Access works well. Conclusion iOS 27 may not bring as many accessibility changes as its predecessor, but several of its additions are substantial. The expanded image-recognition tools can give blind users faster and more independent access to photos, unfamiliar controls, and other visual information, while the new navigation and customization options allow VoiceOver users to better tailor the experience to their needs. Braille users also gain welcome improvements, including more reliable text editing, clearer text-field labels, and support for additional file formats in Braille Access. Some of the most significant new features require Apple Intelligence, leaving users of older compatible devices without access to everything discussed in this article. There are also a few places where braille keyboard support remains incomplete. Even with those limitations, iOS 27 offers a useful collection of accessibility improvements. As always, individual experiences will vary, and readers are encouraged to share their own observations and bugs in the comments. I also encourage users to check out the AppleVis list of bugs and fixes. If needed, more information on how to update the software on your device is available on this Apple Support page. T

en.title: Final Fortress
en.summary: Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress. It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it. Match tiles to finish the day's tasks. Each task brings supplies. Spend them to repair the fortress: reactor, hydroponics, antenna, armory, infirmary. Every repaired system opens new missions. Match 4 or more to charge special tiles. They clear a line, a block, or every tile of one kind. Swap two charged tiles together and they fire as one bigger shape, up to the whole board. The board gets busier as you go: convoy crates that pay out at the bottom, sealed containers with a special tile inside, interference to clear layer by layer, burned sectors the tiles fall past. Some tasks ask for a pattern: decode a sequence in order, or fill a gauge in every column. AI Madness is a mode of its own, outside the fortress. Each shift bends the rules: boards up to 10 by 13, sometimes only three kinds of tile, cascades that barely stop, tasks that may be impossible. On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence, Apple's on-device model (Foundation Models) picks the shift's character and writes its line in the log. Nothing leaves the phone. Otherwise the terminal does the same on its own. Nothing is at stake and nothing is banked. Every shift has a code. Send it to a friend and they get exactly the same board. There is a story in the log: three acts, four threads, and the notes of the commandants who held the fortress before you. It comes a few lines at a time. Read it or skip it. The game never nags about it. Repair the antenna and you will see a board with other players' stations. It is view-only, there is no chat, and it updates once a day. When the story is over, the log keeps going quietly on its own. The music belongs to your fortress alone. The sound is synthesized live and seeded from your fortress, so your station hums like no other and never loops. The hum changes with what is running, with the hour of the night and with the weather outside. Each kind of tile has its own note, and a cascade climbs the scale. One extra room, The Long Dark, carries a call of its own. Three more stations use the instruments in your phone: a weather post that reads the barometer, an acoustic modem and a direction finder. A home screen widget shows your fortress at a glance, in StandBy too. No ads. No lives, timers, energy or streaks. No pop-ups, no push notifications, no accounts, no daily rewards to come back for. Run out of moves and the terminal just says the packet was lost. Try again, nothing is taken away. You can drop a task at any time. Purchases are cosmetic only: screen colors, one extra soundtrack, custom names. Nothing you can buy helps you play, and no purchase moves you up the board. Works offline, on iPhone and iPad. Fully playable with VoiceOver, with a flicker-free stable phosphor mode and a calm mode that softens the board's flashes and haptics.

en.title: One Line Journal app
en.summary: One sentence a day. One book at the end of the year. Your life is happening — quietly, quickly, in small moments. Weekly — Once a week, reflect in 3–5 sentences. Your daily entries appear above for context, so nothing gets lost. Monthly — Write a brief summary that becomes a full chapter in your book. Book View — Watch your year assemble itself in real time — months as chapters, weeks and days woven beneath them. Export — At year's end, export your complete book as Markdown, PDF, or DOCX. BUILT FOR PRIVACY Everything stays on your device. No accounts. No cloud sync. No analytics. Face ID and passcode lock keep your words yours — and auto-lock kicks in the moment you leave the app. THOUGHTFUL DETAILS Highlights to mark the moments worth remembering Tags to thread themes across your year Gentle reminders to keep the habit alive A clean, distraction-free writing interface Simple timeline navigation — no clutter, no feed NO SOCIAL. NO NOTIFICATIONS. NO NOISE. Just you and your words, building something you'll want to read. A year feels long while you're living it. It feels short when you look back. Capture it — one sentence at a time.
