en.title: Surprise and Shine: Recapping Apple's September 9 Announcements
en.summary: Intro Apple has just wrapped up Surprise and Shine, the big fall announcement event. We got new iPhones, Apple Watches, and (non-pro) AirPods. And yes, the rumors were finally true: one of the new iPhones is a folding one. AirPods have some new tricks, the new Apple Watch has some very nice improvements, and even the normal iPhones are worth checking out. Let's get into it. iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo All of the iPhones announced today share a few features, so we'll start there. At the heart of each new iPhone is the A20 Pro, a system on a chip (SoC) that's better than anything Apple has ever made. So said the presenters, anyway. This is Apple's first 2NM chip, which basically means they shrank the parts so they can fit more into the same amount of space, all while using less power and producing less heat. The A20 Pro comes with four efficiency cores and two cores meant to do serious work, which is the same distribution as last year (six cores, with four efficiency and two powerful ones). The big change here is that the two workhorse cores, called super cores, are beefed up considerably. Apple claims they have desktop performance. The graphics chip has also been upgraded, with seven cores and faster access to the phone's RAM; Apple says graphics run up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro. It's 2026, so we can't not talk about AI, specifically large language models. The A20 Pro has neural accelerators to boost AI performance for the CPU and GPU cores, but the star of the show is the neural engine. Or rather, the engines, plural. Each A20 Pro has two of them, not just one, giving the chip 32 neural cores to work with. Combined with the A20's increased access to memory, Apple said that this is the best chip for mobile AI tasks. All of this performance is going to produce a lot of heat, so Apple took the vapor chamber from iPhone 17 Pro and made some improvements. The way the chip's components transfer heat to the chamber is more efficient now, the materials have been updated, and the design has been altered. The new design has three times the space and is made from a combination of titanium and a special copper alloy. It transfers 40% more heat than the system on iPhone 17 Pro, letting the phone do more work for longer before it has to slow itself down to keep from overheating. Remember Siri AI, a version of Siri that is aware of your locations, messages, and other details? It was announced back in June. If you don't follow Apple news as obsessively as I do, the short version is that Siri is far more aware and capable than before. You can ask for "that recipe Jake sent me a couple months ago", you can issue more natural commands, and you can get much more accurate results with dictation. All of this is kept in a new Siri app, so you can check on past conversations. Oh, and Siri's voice is better than ever. Anyway, Siri AI is fully supported by all the new phones, and Apple spent some time reminding us of what all is going to be possible. There are some extra goodies for Apple Watch Series 12 owners who have Siri AI devices, too, but we'll get to those later. iPhone 18 Pro As has become customary, Apple is offering this year's pro phones in standard and Max variants. The Max has the most battery life of any iPhone ever, while the smaller phone has battery life equivalent to what iPhone 17 Pro Max offers. This seems to be the main difference; both have the same chip, camera, design, and everything else, so I'll just talk about iPhone 18 Pro from here on out. Everything also applies to iPhone 18 Pro Max unless I say otherwise. The stand-out feature of the camera system this year is variable aperture. Specially-designed, tiny pieces in the camera can move to let in more or less light, which also changes the field depth. The aperture widens in low light, closes some in bright light, and can be manually adjusted to change the feel of a picture. I guess professional photographers will be jumping for joy. The A20 Pro's AI capabilities also allow Apple to add more camera enhancements, some of which we knew about already from the iOS 27 announcement at WWDC back in June. What is unique to iPhone 18 Pro, though, is a new set of manual camera controls, called pro controls. These let you change the aperture, white balance, and other settings whose purpose I can only guess at. You can even use AI to keep video locked on a subject. But you're not here for camera details, so let's get on with it. There are a few other, smaller changes compared to iPhone 17 Pro. The new phone can charge faster when plugged in (as opposed to using wireless charging). The Dynamic Island is also smaller and now supports up to three live activities at once. Surprisingly, that's about it. The battery life improvements are great, the A20 Pro sounds like an impressive chip, and the colors have changed (silver, black, glacier, and burgundy). Aside from that, faster wired charging, and the camera improvements, everything seems to be the same. Apple didn't mention the screen, body material, any new or changed buttons, speakers, wifi performance, or anything else. It seems iPhone 18 Pro is, physically, the same as iPhone 17 Pro, just with a new chip and camera. You can pre-order iPhone 18 Pro starting September 12, and it will start shipping on September 18. The Pro starts at $1,199, $1,299 for the Pro Max. This gives you 256GB of storage, just like last year. You can upgrade all the way up to 2TB of storage, the first time any iPhone has offered such a large internal drive. Just know that it won't be cheap. You can also check out the new array of colors for Apple's official cases, cross-body straps, and (new this year) wrist straps. iPhone Duo Apple's first entry into the world of foldable phones is called iPhone Duo . It has a 5.4-inch outer display and unfolds to show a 7.6-inch screen. Both screens have full Apple Pencil support, and the outer screen has Ceramic Shield 2. The frame is high-grade titanium, colored either white or night sky. The side button acts how you expect, but also sports a Touch ID sensor--the phone lacks Face ID. You can add multiple fingers, so that no matter how you happen to hold the phone, the finger resting on the button can unlock it. You can also unlock your phone with your watch. Also, despite being foldable, iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating. That means dust and water will have a hard time getting into it, but you shouldn't take it swimming. Each half of iPhone Duo is very, very thin--after all, the whole package has to be comfortably thin when folded. Apple says that each half is the thinnest iPhone ever produced, which suggests that the halves are thinner than an iPhone Air. Despite this, iPhone Duo has good battery life (30 hours of video playback on the internal screen, 44 when using the outer one) and supports fast wired charging. It also, as mentioned earlier, has the same A20 Pro chip and vapor chamber cooling as iPhone 18 Pro. It even has Apple's custom cellular modem, the C2, giving it millimeter wave 5G support (U.S. only for now) and faster and more efficient cellular communications overall. The camera situation is interesting. iPhone Duo sports the same camera system as iPhone 18 Pro, though without the variable aperture feature. When unfolded, an under-screen selfie camera is available, while a more capable camera lives just above the outer screen. This enables some neat options, such as letting both the photographer and the subject see the camera feed (one person on the inner screen, the other on the outer one) before a picture is taken. If you are taking pictures of children, iOS lets you enable animations designed to draw attention and get the kids' eyes looking toward the lens. When making FaceTime calls, someone can use the inner camera and screen, while someone else can use the outer set, letting two people use the same phone but with different camera feeds. Thanks to its design, you can fold iPhone Duo in such a way that the camera stays pointed where you want without being held. You can let iOS monitor the feed, and take the picture when it thinks you're ready. As to the screen, Apple spent a lot of time talking up the engineering that went into minimizing the crease, getting the under-finger feel right, and more. A special coating makes the screen feel closer to glass than the plasticky feel some folding phones have, while also cutting glare and reflections. Nano-scale layers of lenses help the screen stay bright and readable, while reducing the wear of all the folding and unfolding it will undergo during its life. That's not all the engineering that went into iPhone Duo, either. The frame is not only made of titanium, but reinforced at key points with custom materials for added strength. The hinge is weighted, balanced, and carefully structured to fully support the screen at every point of the folding process. You can set the two halves at any angle (up to 180 degrees) and they will stay there. Use it like a small iPad, set one screen at an angle like a laptop while you type on the other one, or make a tent shape, using the phone like a stand while you watch the outer display. The phone will react how you expect, even going so far as to constantly balance the audio coming from its dual speakers based on how the two halves are configured. iOS 27 has been designed to take full advantage of this phone's unique abilities. You can do a lot of the multi-tasking tricks that you can on iPad, such as opening two apps side by side, quickly moving between on-screen apps, showing a list of emails and an open message at once, and more. You can see two home screen pages at once, and your dock is now vertical. Video controls now appear on the side of the screen, rather than the bottom, so videos have more space and so your thumb can reach the controls. The status bar is smaller and now stays in a corner, again, to give apps more room. Apps have new APIs available, letting them, for example, show a list of options on one half of the screen and a preview of the selected option on the other half. iOS will even detect how the phone is being used and move content toward the edge, so it is easier to tap or see. I realize that much of this section has been about cameras, on-screen layouts, and other things that a lot of you reading this won't care about. That's because that was the focus of the presentation. For now, iPhone Duo feels like a device that will be amazing for plenty of sighted users, but will have less appeal to those of us who use VoiceOver. Low vision folks may love the larger screen, but not being such a person myself, I can't really comment on that. Personally, I'm going to see how things go with this phone, play with one in person once my local stores have some, and not worry about getting my own just yet. I don't know if there will be enough advantage for VoiceOver to justify the cost. Of course, it would be nice to have Touch ID again. iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model. As with iPhone 18 Pro, you can increase this all the way to 2TB. Preorders open on October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability starting on October 23. AirPods 5 Today brought us a new AirPods model: AirPods 5 . Like the previous generation, they come in two variants, one more expensive than the other. With AirPods 4, the cheaper model lacked active noise cancelation and wireless charging. That's not the case anymore With this new generation, both variants have ANC. The more expensive AirPods add volume adjustment on the stem, just like AirPods Pro, and a case that supports wireless charging. As we've come to expect, the case can handle MagSafe, Qi, and Apple Watch chargers. The premium version also have a five-hour battery life, which is an hour more than what the less expensive ones offer. This is measured with ANC enabled. Both versions of AirPods 5 are, Apple claims, designed to feel and sound better while lasting longer. ANC is 50% more effective than AirPods 4, while transparency sounds more natural. Audio sounds more detailed and rich, and the earbuds can shrug off more sweat and rain than before. They will also work better in even more ear shapes--so Apple says, anyway. No, they are still not available in any color other than white. The less expensive AirPods cost $129, which is what the non-noise-canceling AirPods 4 cost, and this generation includes ANC. That's a good deal, but for just $20 more, you can get on-stem volume controls and a case that can charge wirelessly. That's $149, which is $30 less expensive than the high-end AirPods 4. Apple isn't known for lowering prices, so this is a very pleasant surprise. You can pre-order starting today (September 9). Deliveries will begin arriving September 18, which is also when stores will start offering the new AirPods. Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 The Apple Watch got some nice enhancements this time around. They all apply equally to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, so I will just talk about the new features here. Everything is true of both models, neither of which seems to have changed, physically, from its predecessor. The first improvement is to the heart sensors. Apple Watch has always used lights to measure your pulse, and that hasn't changed. The LEDs in these new models are different, though. Skin contact is better, the LEDs have been arranged in a ring pattern, and the color of the light has gone from red to green. Add in the new electrical sensors for ECG readings, and Apple Watch has never had a more accurate measure of your heart rate. Almost more exciting is how often Apple Watch now takes heart measurements: every five seconds. This is up to sixty times more often than previous Apple Watches did. Heart rate variability (HRV) is now measured every five minutes, which is a 24 times increase. HRV is an indicator of stress and cardiovascular health, so the more (and more accurate) the readings, the better. This generation of watch has better step length tracking as well, meaning that indoor walks and runs will be measured more accurately than before. Apple also claims that this makes Apple Watch the most accurate step tracker of all the modern wearables. They are therefore adding a step count complication, at long last. What will watchOS do with all this data? Apart from your heart rate complication actually showing your current pulse, Apple has made a series of health data improvements. A readiness score suggests whether you should make today a recovery-focused day or a day during which you can push more. On iPhone, your heart and activity data feed a new Longevity feature. You can see how you are doing over time, how your metrics compare to the average person at your age, and what you could do to improve things. To make this feature more accurate, you can take VO2 max, flexibility, movement, and other tests, all done using your iPhone's cameras and live coaching from the app. You can also purchase bloodwork from Quest for $119, directly through the Health app (U.S. only, for now). The results will inform your health insights and recommendations. You can also connect your existing health records, as has been possible for some time. It's not all about health, though. Audio Intelligence is a set of features centered around the microphones in the watch and Siri AI's increased abilities. All of these features are opt-in, meaning they are not enabled by default. Sound Recognition has been on iPhones for years, but now comes to Apple Watch. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can be alerted to sirens, alarms, doorbells, and other sounds. This works even without iPhone nearby. Live Rewind: double press the digital crown and you get a transcript of the last fifteen seconds of conversation. You can read it, or choose to send it to Siri for further use. During the presentation, they showed a server listing food options, then an Apple Watch user bringing up the list as a transcript. It's not clear if you have to activate this feature each time you want the watch to start paying attention, or if it is always available. Siri Recap is a feature you turn on when you want it, such as during a business meeting or an important conversation. Once the event is over, you turn Recap off again. Siri will generate a title and key points from what it heard, letting you review what was said and jog your memory. I assume this also adds to Siri AI's context, letting you ask questions about what was said in the meeting last week, for instance. Shazam for song detection is nothing new, but it is now automatic (once you turn the feature on). You can always know what song is playing near you, without having to ask Siri to do anything. Apple promised that all of these features run locally or, when they don't, are end-to-end encrypted and have extra security built in. No speakers are ever identified or tagged, no audio is saved, nothing is used for training AI. In fact, audio processed by Apple Watch can't leave the system because of how the S11 SoC is designed. Apple has a whole privacy paper about Audio Intelligence if you want to read more. Speaking of the S11 system, let's go over what we know, which isn't much. We know it has something called an Audio Exclave, which is where audio from the watch's microphones is saved and processed. Audio can't leave this isolated part of the system, which is part of how Apple guarantees that Audio Intelligence puts privacy first. The S11 also supports the greatly increased health sensor readings without impacting battery life. Beyond that, Apple made no claims about speed increases, wireless changes or anything else. In a bit of a surprise move, Apple has kept prices the same. The Series 12 starts as $399 for the aluminum casing, while the Ultra starts at $799. Preorders are open today (September 9) and, as with most of what we've talked about here, deliveries and in-store availability start on September 18. The new colors and materials are: aluminum, now with Ceramic Shield 2 glass: black, space gray, light gold, and dark bronze ceramic: pearl white and night blue titanium (Series 12): radiant gold and natural titanium (Apple Watch Ultra 4): black and natural That's All For Now Rumors continue to swirl that Apple has more to show us, so there might be press releases or another event later this year. For now, though, we've covered all the new shinies--iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5. Plus, version 27 of all of Apple's operating systems comes out on September 14, at which time we will finally get a look at this much-improved Siri that all these new devices were built to support. What caught your metaphorical eye, if anything? Personally, I pre-ordered a Series 12 before I was halfway done writing this article. It'll be a big upgrade over my SE 3, and since most of what I use my Apple Watch for is health-related, I want all the data I can get. I might see about AirPods 5 if a good sale comes along, but I'll wait for the reviews. I like the idea of a folding phone, and I definitely want to play with one in person, but I have no desire to own one. I'm also not planning to get an iPhone 18 Pro, though if Siri AI and upcoming Apple Intelligence features turn out to be as amazing as Apple insists they are, well, we'll see. What do you think? Discuss your excitement, bitter disappointment, or indifference in the comments!

en.title: ghostWriter Markdown
en.summary: Accessibility-first Markdown writing with VoiceOver-friendly editing, document organization, and flexible exports to Word, PDF, HTML, braille, and more. ghostWriter Markdown is a plain-text writing app for notes, articles, lists, documentation, and anything else you want to say with words. It was built accessibility-first. Not accessibility-eventually, or accessibility-in-the-settings-somewhere. VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code, as the app has been fully created by a Blind developer. If you write with a screen reader, this app was made for you. If you don't, you get a clean, fast, native editor that never gets in your way. So what's Markdown? Markdown adds structure to writing using a few ordinary punctuation marks. A number sign makes a heading. A dash makes a list item. Your document stays readable as plain text, and you can render it whenever you want to see the finished formatting. You don't have to know any of this to start. The Insert feature can add common elements for you, and a built-in Markdown Reference is always a tap away. Writing Made Easy: • A native editor with the Markdown punctuation kept visible, so you always control the source • Insert Actions for links, images, headings, quotes, code, lists, tasks, tables, and rules • Automatic list continuation for bullets, numbers, and task lists • Indent and outdent with tabs or spaces, your choice • Find and Replace, dictation, braille input, and text selection through native iOS controls • A configurable Status Bar showing line, column, word count, current heading, and selection • Automatic saving as you pause, plus Save Now whenever you want it Useful Navigation: • Outline lists every heading in your document and jumps straight to one, moving both the cursor and VoiceOver focus • A 3-finger horizontal swipe with VoiceOver will move the cursor through your document headings while editing • Jump to Line for long documents • Search across document names and their contents • Your last editing position is remembered in every file Keep Files Organized: • Nested folders you can create, rename, move, and navigate • Pin the documents you keep coming back to • Sort by name, created, modified, or last opened • Recently Deleted holds removed files until you restore them or clear them out • Import Markdown, .txt, Word .docx or Powerpoint presentations to convert them into Markdown Render and Share: • See your Markdown as structured HTML right inside the app • Share complete standalone HTML, Markdown, plain text, ePub, tagged PDF, eBraille, BRF, Microsoft Word documents or even Powerpoint presentations • Rendered output uses real semantic headings, lists, tables, links, and landmarks — so what you share is accessible to whoever receives it Your Files, Your Devices: • Documents are ordinary Markdown files, visible in the Files app • Store them on your device, or turn on iCloud Drive to sync across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac • Open and edit the same files in any other app that reads text • Nothing is locked in a proprietary format, and nothing needs this app to survive Accessibility: Developed toward WCAG 2.2 Level AA and tested with VoiceOver as a primary interaction method. • A predictable, linear VoiceOver reading order • Native controls with the roles and behaviors you already expect • Dynamic Type, including accessibility text sizes, everywhere • System, monospaced, rounded, and serif editor typefaces • Light, dark, and system appearance • Voice Control, Switch Control, and hardware keyboard support • Optional keyboard shortcuts for common actions • Reduced-motion support Privacy: No accounts. No sign-in. No ads. No analytics. No tracking. No data collection of any kind. There is no server behind this app because there doesn't need to be one. Your documents are yours, on your device or in your own iCloud, and they never travel anywhere you don't send them. Made by a blind developer who got tired of using tools that treated screen reader support as an afterthought. Heading

Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. Y lo mejor de todo: traduce incluso archivos grandes como libros enteros. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres. Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir. 6. Selector de idiomas del OCR (Tesseract) completo En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. Requisitos para utilizar TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: • Windows10 (x64) en adelante. • portable, sin instalación. • Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline • Para Google Translate: conexión a internet Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión. Tutorial: 📘 TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: OCR en PDF, 🚀 traduce libros y más! En este tutorial les mostraré: • Les mostraré la nueva conversión de Docx a PDF. • Conversión de PPTX a Markdown. • Conversión de un PDF (que son imágenes) a un PDF accesible (que admite búsqueda). • Construir un archivo PDF a partir de imágenes Jpg o PNG. • Muestra de que todos los idiomas ahora se cargan en el Motor OCR Tesseract. • Como traducir un documento en formato TXT a otro idioma de forma Online usando Google Translate (• conversión del inglés al español). • Como traducir un documento en formato Docx, utilizando la traducción OfLine con Argos Translate (• muestra del inglés al francés, descarga de idiomas y más). • Finalmente les mostraré, como traducir un PDF a otro idioma. New Apps AudioReel From the App Store: Ever had an audio clip you wanted to post on social media, but couldn't because it's just an audio file? en.title: Apple Introduces Updated Mac Mini and Mac Studio with Upgraded Chips and Improved Connectivity
en.summary: Apple today updated the Mac mini and Mac Studio, introducing the M6 Chip for the Mac mini, as well as the M5 Ultra Chip for the Mac Studio, which Apple describes as its "most powerful silicon ever." Mac mini The new Mac mini with M6 delivers up to 4x faster AI performance, up to 2x faster graphics and storage, and Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5 gigabit Ethernet connectivity, according to Apple's press release for the Mac Mini . Apple lists the following additional claims related to the Mac Mini with M6: Up to 13.5x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M1, and up to 4.8x faster than M4. Up to 2.3x faster spreadsheet calculations in Microsoft Excel when compared to Mac mini with M1, and up to 1.5x faster than M4. Up to 2x faster gaming performance with ray tracing in Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition when compared to Mac mini with M4. In addition to the M6, the Mac mini is also available with M5 Pro, which Apple claims delivers: Up to 8.5x faster LLM prompt processing performance in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 4x faster than M4 Pro. Up to 4.5x faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 1.4x faster than M4 Pro. Up to 2.1x faster image processing in Affinity when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 1.5x faster than M4 Pro. Besides the upgraded chips, the new Mac mini features Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5GB Ethernet by default (up from the prior generation's default 1GB Ethernet port), with a 10GB option available. The new Mac mini can be preordered from Apple today for a starting price of US $899, and will begin shipping on Tuesday, September 22. Mac Studio Apple has also updated the Mac Studio, bringing the M5 Max and new M5 Ultra chip to Apple's most high-end Mac, as well as Thunderbolt 5, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 6 connectivity, and a "next-generation SSD architecture that is up to twice as fast as before," according to Apple's press release for the Mac Studio The new Mac Studio with M5 Max delivers up to 3.9x faster AI performance than the prior generation, with the M5 Ultra delivering up to 4.3x the peak AI performance of the M3 Ultra, and up to 9.8x the peak AI performance of the M1 Ultra. Apple additionally lists the following claims related to Mac Studio with M5 Max: Up to 10.7x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and 3.9x faster than M4 Max. Up to 7.4x faster text-to-image performance when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3.5x faster than M4 Max. Up to 5.3x faster Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3x faster than M4 Max. Up to 3.5x faster basecalling for DNA sequencing in Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 1.9x faster than M4 Max. In addition to the M5 Max, the new Mac Studio is available with the new M5 Ultra, which Apple claims delivers: Up to 15.4x faster CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 3.3x faster than M3 Ultra. Up to 9.8x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4x faster than M3 Ultra. Up to 8.2x faster text-to-image performance when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4.3x faster than M3 Ultra. Up to 4.7x faster scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 1.7x faster than M3 Ultra. In addition, the Mac Studio with M5 Ultra is available with up to 512 GB of unified memory with 1.2TB/S of memory bandwidth, 50% higher memory bandwidth than M3 Ultra. The new Mac Studio can be preordered from Apple today for a starting price of US $2,499, and most models will begin shipping on Tuesday, September 22, with the model with 512GB of memory shipping in late October.

Seguramente ya lo han vivido: hay programas que no descargan, otros que si descargan el archivo queda sin sonido, o que directamente lanzan errores al intentar reproducir. Y esto no es un problema exclusivo de estas versiones ni de estos programas. La causa real son los constantes cambios que realiza YouTube y otras plataformas, que modifican su funcionamiento con frecuencia para dificultar las descargas externas. Por ese motivo, la librería yt-dlp debe estar constantemente adaptándose a dichos cambios, lanzando parches que a veces llegan antes y a veces llegan tarde, y esos cambios rompen muchas funciones hasta que llega la solución. Muy atentos. Hoy les traigo la actualización de TCA-TTS-TIMMER, nuestro querido reloj parlante para Windows, que llega a la versión 1.2 cargada de novedades muy importantes y funcionalidades útiles! Antes, para quienes no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA-TTS-TIMMER? Es una pequeña utilidad desarrollada en Python que nos permite escuchar la hora cada 15 minutos, 30 minutos o cada hora, mediante un sonido y una voz TTS. Además, puede darnos la hora de muchos países de Latinoamérica y Europa, todo desde una interfaz sencilla, totalmente accesible y con atajos de teclado. Novedades en TCA-TTS-TIMMER 1.2 El reloj llega a la versión 1.2 con los siguientes cambios: • Hora Universal UTC Ahora el reloj incorpora un botón en la interfaz principal que te permite saber la Hora Universal UTC al instante. Disponible también mediante el atajo de teclado Alt+U. Muy útil para quienes trabajan con sistemas, servidores o simplemente necesitan la referencia horaria internacional. • Nueva voz: Español México (mx) Además de la voz español España, ahora incorporamos la voz español México (mx). Podrás elegir entre ambas desde el cuadro combinando "Lenguaje de la voz" en las opciones. Una voz clara y agradable que le da un toque diferente al reloj. • Alarmas ¡TCA-TTS-TIMMER ahora permite establecer alarmas! Desde el botón "Alarmas" en la interfaz principal, podrás gestionar una o varias alarmas al día, eligiendo la hora, el sonido y el número de repeticiones. Ideal para recordatorios, descansos o lo que necesites. • Apagado programado Otra función muy solicitada: el apagado programado. Puedes programar que tu PC se apague automáticamente después de un número determinado de horas y minutos. Perfecto para cuando dejas el equipo realizando una tarea por la noche o antes de salir de casa. También incluye un botón para cancelar el apagado si cambias de opinión. • Correcciones y mejoras internas Se realizaron varias correcciones y mejoras en el código para un funcionamiento más estable y eficiente. Compatibilidad El programa es compatible con Windows 10 en adelante, para 64 bits. En versiones antiguas de Windows, puede que necesites las librerías Visual Studio C++ (incluidas en la descarga). Tutorial: ⏰ TCA TTS Timmer 1.2: Alarmas, UTC , Apagado programado y +! He grabado un video tutorial donde muestro todas estas novedades en acción: • El nuevo botón de Hora UTC y su atajo Alt+U. • Cómo cambiar a la voz mexicana y escucharla anunciar la hora. • Cómo configurar y gestionar alarmas. • Cómo usar el apagado programado paso a paso. La descarga. Les dejaré en la descarga: • El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial). • El programa TCA-TTS-TIMMER 1.2 para 64 bits. • Las librerías Visual Studio C++. Descargador de Música Accesible 1.4.2 : Otra gran alternativa inclusiva para YouTube Introducción En el mundo actual, el contenido multimedia es parte fundamental de nuestro día a día. Para la comunidad de personas con discapacidad visual, contar con herramientas que permitan descargar y gestionar este contenido de forma autónoma es vital. Si bien ya existen en el ecosistema opciones consolidadas y muy queridas como TCA MediaDownloader, siempre es una excelente noticia recibir nuevas propuestas que enriquezcan nuestras opciones. Hoy queremos hablar de Descargador de Música Accesible, otra fantástica alternativa que se suma a la lista de herramientas diseñadas desde cero para garantizar una experiencia fluida, cómoda y sin barreras. Esta aplicación ha sido desarrollada por Nicolás Alfaro, programador y miembro del colectivo de personas con discapacidad visual, quien ha puesto su conocimiento al servicio de la comunidad. ¿Qué es Descargador de Música Accesible? Es una aplicación gratuita para Windows que permite bajar audio y video desde YouTube de manera sencilla y con total compatibilidad con lectores de pantalla. Actualmente en su versión 1.4.2, el programa destaca por su ligereza y por integrar soluciones prácticas —como un reproductor interno portable— que facilitan la navegación previa a la descarga. Al ser un proyecto creado por y para usuarios con discapacidad visual, cada ventana y comando está optimizado para responder exactamente a lo que la comunidad necesita, convirtiéndose en un complemento ideal para tu día a día digital. Características principales • Interfaz 100% accesible: Diseñada minuciosamente para funcionar a la perfección con NVDA y JAWS. Cada elemento, botón y cuadro de diálogo está correctamente etiquetado para una navegación fluida mediante el tabulador y atajos de teclado. • Buscador integrado de YouTube: No necesitas abrir el navegador. El programa incluye una pestaña de búsqueda directa que ofrece hasta 50 resultados, permitiéndote elegir el contenido exacto desde una lista cómoda y accesible. • Reproductor interno MPV: Una de las novedades más potentes de la versión 1.4.2. Incorpora un reproductor basado en MPV portable para escuchar el audio o ver el video antes de descargarlo, con controles adaptados y accesibles. • Variedad de formatos y calidades: Audio (MP3): Permite elegir entre calidades de 128, 256 y 320 kbps. Video (MP4). • Información detallada antes de descargar: Puedes verificar el título, duración, fecha de publicación y número de visualizaciones para asegurarte de que es el archivo correcto. • Historial de descargas: Un registro organizado y accesible desde el menú superior para revisar tus archivos obtenidos recientemente. Mantenimiento y actualización integrada: Como YouTube actualiza su plataforma constantemente, el programa incluye una opción en el menú de herramientas para actualizar las librerías de yt-dlp de forma automática, garantizando que el software nunca quede obsoleto. • Sistema de diagnóstico: Si experimentas fallos con el lector de pantalla o el reproductor, la app cuenta con una herramienta de diagnóstico que verifica el estado de NVDA y los módulos de Python. Puedes exportar este reporte para recibir soporte técnico de forma eficiente. Contacto y soporte El desarrollo de software accesible crece gracias a la retroalimentación de la comunidad. Si tienes sugerencias, comentarios o deseas reportar algún fallo, puedes ponerte en contacto directo con el desarrollador: Correo electrónico: alfaronico8@gmail.com Nota para el soporte: Se recomienda ser lo más detallado posible al describir cualquier incidencia o sugerencia para facilitar las futuras actualizaciones del programa.
